findings.description: Profile/context switch (reloadActiveProfile) does not clear triggerHeldState or cancel active trigger jobs. If user holds a trigger (e.g. for voice dictation) and accidentally presses the context-cycle button, the trigger state becomes desynchronized with the new profile's action mappings. Example: Context A maps TRIGGER_L2 to VOICE_TRIGGER; user holds trigger -> recording starts. User presses CYCLE_CONTEXT -> switches to Context B where TRIGGER_L2 maps to SCROLL. User releases trigger -> handleTrigger sees state change but resolves action=SCROLL, calls stopTriggerRepeat() instead of pttController.onButtonUp(). PttController.isHeld stays true, recording continues until MAX_RECORDING_MS (30s) timeout or user presses trigger again (which triggers double-press cancel). Fix: call cancelAllTriggerJobs() in reloadActiveProfile() to reset trigger state on profile change.

Hysteresis implementation in isTriggerActive() is correct: press threshold 0.5f, release threshold 0.25f creates a 0.25 dead zone. The logic `if (currentlyActive) value >= releaseThreshold else value >= pressThreshold` properly implements asymmetric thresholds. ControllerAccessibilityService.handleTrigger() correctly tracks per-trigger state in triggerHeldState map and only acts on state transitions. This fixes the reported STT sentence corruption where analog noise near a single 0.4 threshold sliced one hold into multiple truncated recordings.

VoiceBridgeServer generates per-instance authToken (line 46) but token is never exposed to any client — started in ControllerAccessibilityService.onServiceConnected() but not logged, stored, or shared via IPC. Comment states 'Give this only to the trusted in-process caller' but no mechanism exists to pass it. Pre-existing known issue (declined in rounds 6, 7, 8 as F5/RV2/F1). If endpoint is for local testing/debugging, legitimate clients cannot authenticate. If for internal future use, should be documented or auth removed.

REV=3 migration (lines 70-78) discards ALL user-customized button mappings from legacy profiles (rev < 3), keeping only tuning values (sensitivity/deadzone/cursorEnabled/invertScroll). Breaking data-loss change for existing users. Acknowledged as acceptable for AntiMicroX parity but must be explicitly documented in release notes. Pre-existing known issue (declined in rounds 6, 7, 8 as F3/RV3/F2).

styleLabel() logic duplicated in FloatingKeyboardOverlay (line 319), AIInputMethodService (line 129), and KeyboardActivity (line 89). commitStyledChar() per-character styling logic also triplicated across all three keyboards (FloatingKeyboardOverlay line 488, AIInputMethodService line 295, KeyboardActivity line 227). Violates DRY and creates maintenance risk. Pre-existing known issue (declined in rounds 6, 7, 8 as F4/RV4/F4). Consider extracting to TextStyles or shared helper.

PttController implements double-press cancel: second ACTION_DOWN while isHeld=true calls onCancel() and resets state (lines 28-35). New behavior not in Linux ptt_pynput.py original. User holding trigger who accidentally presses again (or noisy trigger edge) cancels recording without warning. With hysteresis fix, accidental double-press from noise is less likely (requires crossing 0.5->0.25->0.5), but intentional/accidental double-press still triggers cancel. Pre-existing known issue (declined in rounds 7, 8 as RV6/F3).

KeyboardActivity lacks font size controls (A+/A- with KeyboardFontSizeStore), skin tone picker (🎨), voice button, and punctuation row that FloatingKeyboardOverlay and AIInputMethodService have. Labeled 'Open Legacy Keyboard (diagnostic)' in MainActivity, so minimalism may be intentional. If meant as fallback, missing features should be documented. Pre-existing known issue (declined in rounds 6, 7, 8 as F6/RV5/F5).

testing_summary: Unable to run compilation/tests due to missing Android SDK in environment. Review based on static analysis of source changes only.
risk_rationale: Core hysteresis fix (HYS-2) is correct and addresses the stated intent. However, HYS-1 introduces a concrete bug where context switching while holding a trigger desynchronizes trigger state, potentially leaving voice recording running indefinitely. This is a new bug introduced by the broader feature changes in this branch. Other findings are pre-existing known issues previously declined by the user.
